text:
Maria (support): Hey team — customer on Dedicated reports intermittent 429s despite being well under their committed qps. Happens during longer streaming responses, not simple short generations. They see gaps of ~30–90s then normal traffic returns.

Sam (sre): Copy — do we have any headers or sample responses from the client when a 429 occurs? Any x-req-id?

Maria (support): Pasted from the client: 

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Request-Id: req_01Gx4Y2Z
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset: 24
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "detail": "reserved_pool_depleted" }

Also attaching short server log snippet from their tenant (redacted ids):

[2026-03-16T18:21:12Z] tenant=t-451 stream_conn=abc123 tokens_used=1200 pool_remaining=0 action=throttle code=429
[2026-03-16T18:21:13Z] tenant=t-451 stream_conn=abc123 reason=refill_mismatch
[2026-03-16T18:21:45Z] tenant=t-451 stream_conn=abc123 tokens_recovered=200 pool_remaining=200 allow=true

Sam (sre): Interesting — pool_remaining hitting 0 then refilling slowly matches a token-bucket refill mismatch rather than an auth glitch. Is the customer's workload long-lived streams that keep KV caches and generate tokens incrementally?

Maria (support): Yes — it's a chat-like workflow where each response streams ~200–800 tokens, and they run ~6 parallel streams. They have a reserved pool contract for 2k tokens/sec but their per-route shaping seems to expect steady bursts.

Jordan (infra): Two hypotheses: 1) Their reserved pool is sized as a steady rate but streaming responses keep connections open and consume tokens with low concurrency but high per-response token counts, which can temporarily exhaust the bucket; 2) Our rate-handshake windows (soft cap vs hard cap) are misaligned with the customer's token accounting — e.g., token credit is applied per-request completion not per-stream-chunk.

Sam (sre): Can we get a quick repro script from them? Ask them to run this locally and paste the response headers when they see a 429: 

```bash
for i in {1..12}; do \
  curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-dedicated-v1","stream":true,"input":"long response test"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate || true 
  sleep 1
done
```

Jordan (infra): Also request the X-Redwood-* headers for the failing requests. I want to see X-Redwood-Pool-Remaining and X-Redwood-Pool-Refill-At if present. If they don't expose those, we can pull telemetry server-side once they share tenant id.

Maria (support): Customer provided tenant id t-451 already. I'll ask them to run the script and send headers. They are worried about billing if we enable larger bursts.

Sam (sre): Quick note on billing: reserved pool consumption counts against their reserved capacity first. If we configure burst > reserved, those extra tokens are billed on-demand. We can temporarily enable a small burst window to avoid 429s while we tune, but need explicit customer opt-in.

Maria (support): Customer asked what a "small burst window" means. 

Jordan (infra): Operationally: we have two knobs — soft_burst_window (permits short lived exceed of reservation up to X tokens for Y seconds) and hard_cap which rejects. For triage set soft_burst_window=500 tokens over 30s for their pool and monitor pool_remaining. That should smooth out 1–2 big responses.

Sam (sre): For root cause, GA: check if token attribution is delayed until stream close. If credits are only refunded/reconciled at end-of-request, concurrent streams can appear to use more than realtime. Add these checks: 
- correlate stream_conn id to token debit events in infra logs
- check refill_rate vs observed token_recovered events
- check any recent config changes to per-route shaping (rolled last week?)

Maria (support): Customer ran the repro and returned these headers when it failed: 

X-Redwood-Request-Id: req_01Gx4Y2Z
X-Redwood-Pool-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-Pool-Refill-Sec: 18
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset: 18

They also showed that after 20s, Pool-Remaining jumped to ~400 and next request succeeded.

Jordan (infra): That strongly suggests refill granularity is larger than their inter-request spacing. Two mitigation paths: 1) short term: increase soft_burst_window for t-451 and advise customer to reduce per-stream token size or stagger starts; 2) long term: change per-chunk accounting so partial stream chunks are debited as they are emitted (more accurate realtime accounting). The latter is an infra work item.

Sam (sre): Create an internal ticket and tag eng-runtime for per-chunk accounting work. For immediate customer relief, Maria — offer the soft burst change with billing note: "we'll enable a 30s/500-token soft burst. Any consumption beyond reserved during that window will be charged at on-demand rates; we can revert after monitoring."

Maria (support): Customer accepted the temporary change and asked for monitoring. I'll set up a dashboard for t-451 showing pool_remaining, refill_rate, 429 count and a simple alert if 429s > 3 in 10m.

eng-bot: Deploy request created: deploy/soft-burst/t-451 (change: soft_burst_window=30s, soft_burst_tokens=500). CI pipeline -> canary -> prod. Correlation id deploy_9002.

Sam (sre): After deployment, collect a 10-minute pcap of request headers and correlate to infra logs for stream_conn abc123. Also note the customer is close to their monthly reserved commit; if they keep bursting we'll need to discuss commit bump to avoid sustained on-demand billing.

Jordan (infra): I'll own the engineering ticket for per-chunk accounting. Assigning to @infra-team. TODOs: reproduce with unit tests, measure overhead, design migration.

Maria (support): Closing loop with customer now. Thanks all — will update ticket with repro script output and headers.

Sam (sre): Thanks — keep me posted if 429s persist after soft burst. We'll escalate to live debugging if needed.
